what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources folder: scripts the person's AI runs on the person's own computer to check a narrator's claims against the person's world rows and sources, and to make the plain-text extracts of those sources.

payload.label: Check every claim my narrator makes, spoken or on screen, against my facts and sources before it is voiced (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Check every sentence my narrator says and every text on screen against the facts I keep and the sources I cite, and tell me which claims fail and why
payload.description: Reads a run's shots (shots/<id>.json: the voice script and the on-screen events), their claims files (claims/<id>.json: one entry per spoken sentence and per on-screen text, each citing world facts, source wordings, transcript quotes or saved frames), the person's world rows (lists.json, rows/<list>.json, relations.json: entities, facts and relations) and their sources file with its plain-text extracts. The world's own check runs first (row shapes, links, roles, every fact's words at its transcript second or file line); then each shot fails a claim that: is not covered (script or screen text without an entry, or an entry for nothing); is about the subject but has no support said by someone other than the narrator; ignores a world fact on one of its topics; quotes a source or transcript that does not hold the words; is stronger than its source on a strength scale; says a number not derived from its cited numbers or outside its qualifier; breaks a bound a world fact sets; makes a comparison the numbers do not hold; counts a number in another container than its source; says something is visible without a saved frame; uses a private, believed, past or planned fact without saying so, a claim not recorded as its speaker's statement, or a conflicting fact it has not weighed; or carries a hedge or attribution phrase. Every rule word (strength scales, qualifiers, subject words, labels, tense markers, quantity units) is the person's settings, and the hedge phrases are their no-hedge check row's words. Prints each shot's report lines to standard error and one JSON answer.

request.description: The request JSON file, put where {request} is in the command: {shots, lane_dir, sources, frames_root, world_dir, hedge_phrases, settings_record, settings?, path_map?, check_world?, quiet?}. settings_record is the person's list:settings row record:setting:check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources~<scope_kind>~<scope_id> as records:read gives it (or its id, read through the records door by tools/settings run-with-settings.mjs); its settings hold rules, subject_name, narrator_name and hedge_row, and the request's own settings object lays over them. README.md: Request and Rules.

output_schema.description: Last line {"result": {"ok", "shots": [{"id", "ok", "fails", "notes", "lines"}], "world": {"ok", "lines"}}} with exit 0 when every shot passes and 1 when one fails, or {"error": "what to change"} with exit 2.

needs: the person's world rows, sources, shots and claims files
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request with the folders of the shots and claims to check, the person's world rows and sources file, the words of their no-hedge check row as hedge_phrases, and their settings row (as records:read gives it, or its id) as settings_record. Run `run` and read the last line: each failing shot lists what fails and why. A failing claim is cut or rewritten with real support; never fix it by adding a hedge or an attribution. Render or voice a line only when its shot passes.

provenance.source: Moved from a film repository's films/<film>/narrator/tools/fact_gate.py and test_fact_gate.py, with the parts of library/world/world.py it used; the rules, names and hedge list became the person's settings and rows

payload.label: Make the plain-text copy of every source my claims cite, from the files I saved (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Turn every source I saved for fact checking (a web page, a FoodData Central food, an edit plan, a text) into the plain text my claims are checked against
payload.description: Reads a sources file ({"sources": {id: {raw, extract, text}}}) and writes each source's plain-text extract beside it: html (scripts and styles dropped, tags removed, entities decoded, spaces joined), fdc-json (a FoodData Central food as one line per nutrient amount per 100 g), new-order (an edit plan's new_order rows as one line each) or copy. A kind made by its own tool (a word-timed transcript, a text) keeps its extract and is refused when it is missing. Run it after adding or re-fetching a source; tool:check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources checks quotes against these extracts.

request.description: The request JSON file, put where {request} is: {"sources": the sources file}. Raw and text paths are relative to its folder or absolute.

output_schema.description: Last line {"result": {"sources": [{"id", "text", "chars" | "kept"}]}} or {"error": "what to change"} with exit 2.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout, on the person's sources file. Read the last line: each source's extract and its length, or what to change.

provenance.source: Moved from a film repository's films/<film>/narrator/tools/fact_sources.py; the sources folder is the request's file instead of where the script sat
